line: I was in the flats when the land slanged goals Ridin’ up Satchel when them boys slanged hoes

meaning:
The “Flats” is an informal name of an area on or near the west side of Cleveland, Ohio. The Flats is where people find entertainment, diners, bars, hotels, and a public park. This area has a lot of history, but its attraction went down hill sometime after the new millennium.

The phrase “the land slanged goals” can have multiple interpretations:


Perhaps MGK was saying he was having fun at the Flats during the time Cleveland had its own NHL team, hence the term “goal.”
It is much more probable that MGK was saying that he was having fun at the Flats during the time the area was still a major attraction in Cleveland. There were multiple attempts at reviving this level of attraction, hence, slanging goals.
Another interpretation is that Cleveland had goals of improving–whether that be in economics, education, or social activities–before the United States experienced a recession.



When he said “Ridin' up Satchel when them boys slanged hoes,” he was probably saying that girls were being pimped on a street or area called Satchel.

line: Law #1: never underestimate the enemy See this a very important law Law 2: if a man show a flaw that mean that flaw really exist Never take it for granted never Rule #3: make sure you never break it never sleep where the sack at
vault_lines: Law #1: never underestimate the enemy
meaning:
In the intro, Gotti further deepens his message from his previous track, “Law” to talk  about the art of hustling and the success and tribulations that come with it.

The first law focuses on a concept made by Lao Tzu, an ancient Chinese philospher who thinks that one shouldn’t underestimate the power of the opponent because every enemy offers a potential threat and should be acknowledged for.

The second law is simply saying that if one has a flaw that flaw in them really exists and should be noted that they have a weakness.

The third law is an innuendo on the same notion of what The Notorious B.I.G. claimed in his hit-song, “Ten Crack Commandments”. Biggie stated:

Number 5: never sell no crack where you rest at

Using this logic, Gotti claims that having comfort is inherently dangerous for a drug dealer. To get caught sleeping in the same place you store your drugs, leaves you to vulnerable to the police capture and robbers.

meaning:
Jeezy uses extensive wordplay to illustrate his skill with dealing drugs and making money. He first describes taking a quarter ounce, or “4,” of pure cocaine—often packaged in a way the resembles a “brick”—to make crack cocaine, which looks like crumbled chalk.

He then suggests that he handles so much crack and money that he might as well be a chalk board, which is often made in green. He wraps up by comparing himself to an executive board at a company, which are the people who make the most money—CEOs, CFOs, chairmen, etc.

line: I just had a epiphany, I need to go to Tiffany’s Fendi on my slippers and my cookie’s always slippery I don’t need help, I pay the bills on time So I be yellin’ “Fuck ’em” with a dildo sign
vault_lines: I just had a epiphany, I need to go to Tiffany's
meaning:
“I just had an epiphany, I need to go to Tiffany’s”

She’s saying she suddenly realized (“epiphany”) she deserves luxury — specifically Tiffany & Co., a symbol of wealth and high-class jewelry.
It’s a flex: “I’m rich, I shop where rich women shop.”

“Fendi on my slippers and my cookie’s always slippery”
• Fendi on my slippers = she’s wearing designer even in the house, showing constant luxury.
• “My cookie’s always slippery” = sexual wordplay.
• “Cookie” = her vagina.
• “Slippery” = she’s always aroused, desirable, and sexually powerful.
It’s Nicki using a playful, confident sexual bar to assert femininity and control.

“I don’t need help, I pay the bills on time”

She’s emphasizing her independence.
• She doesn’t rely on men, labels, or anyone else.
    • She makes her money and handles her business like a boss.

This sets up her persona as a woman who’s self-made and self-sufficient.

“So I be yellin’ ‘Fuck ’em’ with a dildo sign”

This is classic Nicki wordplay — funny but sharp.
• “Fuck ’em” = forget the haters, she doesn’t care.
• “With a dildo sign” = a double-meaning.
• Literally: a dildo is used for “fuck” / “fucking.”
    • Figuratively: it means she’s flipping people off in the most disrespectful, exaggerated way.

She’s basically saying:
“I don’t need men, money, or approval — so I tell everyone doubting me to go fuck themselves.”

The absurd image (a “dildo sign”) is part of Nicki’s signature animated, cartoonish rap persona she used heavily in her early career.

How these connect to the 5-star / 3-star line

All these bars build a boss, luxury, independent, sexual, confident persona — so when she calls another woman “three-star,” it hits harder. She’s proving why she’s five-star.

line: Five, little mama, you a three-star
vault_lines: Five, little mama, you a three-star
meaning:
When Nicki says “Five, lil’ mama, you a three-star,” she’s using a rating system as a metaphor for status and quality.
• “Five” refers to five-star, the highest level — top-tier beauty, success, luxury, skill, or fame.
• Calling the other girl “a three-star” means she’s basic, mid-level, not on Nicki’s tier.
    • Nicki is basically saying, “I’m five stars, you’re three. I’m luxury, you’re average. I’m the elite version; you don’t rank where I rank.”

In rap terms, it’s a flex — a way of asserting superiority without having to spell it out.

Even though “lil’ mama” is a common phrase, Nicki knows listeners will hear it as a double-meaning:
1.  Lil Mama is the name of a real rapper — and during the era when Nicki said this, Lil Mama was often criticized, clowning-wise, for being more “cute/pop” than “top-tier rap star.”
2.  By saying:
“Five, lil’ mama, you a three-star”
Nicki creates a subtle name-drop diss:
• Nicki = five-star (top level)
• Lil Mama = three-star (mid, not elite, not on Nicki’s level)
3.  It fits Nicki’s pattern of light jabs at other female rappers without explicitly naming them — the kind of “you know who I mean” subliminal.
4.  Lil Mama was also not seen as competition in the same lane as Nicki. That makes the “three-star” label even harsher:
• It implies Lil Mama’s music, image, and status are lower grade in the hierarchy.
5.  Even if Nicki didn’t mean it as a full diss, the line can be interpreted as shade, because:
• She used the exact phrase “lil mama”, not “shorty,” “girl,” or “chick.”
    • She connects that phrase to a rating scale that downgrades the person.

In short:

Nicki is flexing her status while tossing a subtle jab at Lil Mama — calling herself five-star quality and reducing Lil Mama to a three-star at best. It’s a slick, subliminal diss that fits rap battle culture.
